Original Russian Text © A.G. Iosifidi, V.V. Popov, 2017, published in Fizika Zemli, 2017, No. 5, pp. 3–18.
Paleomagnetism of Permian Rocks of the Subpolar Urals,
Kozhim River: to the History of Evolution of the Thrust Structures
in the Subpolar Urals
A. G. Iosifidi* and V. V. Popov**
All-Russia Petroleum Research Exploration Institute (VNIGRI), St. Petersburg, 191014 Russia
*e-mail: iosag@mail.ru
**e-mail: v_v_popov@yahoo.co.uk
Received May 14, 2015
Abstract⎯ The collections of Permian rocks from sections of the Kozhim River (Asselian, Kungurian, and
Ufimian stages) and the Kama River (Ufimian and Kazanian stages) are studied. The paleomagnetic direc-
tions determined on the studied structures closely agree with the existing data for the Subpolar Urals and Rus-
sian Platform (RP). In the Middle Permian red clays of the Kama River region, the paleomagnetic pole
N/n= 28/51, Φ = 47° N, Λ = 168° E, dp = 3°, and dm = 5° is obtained. The analysis of the existing paleo-
magnetic determinations for the Early and Middle Permian of the Russian and Siberian platforms and
Kazakhstan blocks (KBs) is carried out. For the Subpolar Ural sections, the estimates are obtained for the
local rotations during the collision of the Uralian structures with the Russian and Siberian platforms and KBs.
The amplitudes of the horizontal displacements of the studied structures are, on average, 170 ± 15 km per
Middle Permian. The scenario describing the evolution of the horizontal rotations of the structures of Sub-
polar Urals is suggested.
Keywords: thrusts, paleomagnetic belts, horizontal rotations, anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility, Subpolar Urals
DOI: 10.1134/S1069351317040048
